correctness.rationale: PASS. For the two explicitly given skew matrices and θ interval, minimizing the bilinear margin separately over pure opposing alternatives and interval endpoints yields V_r(p)=min{-ru[(1-z)/2+|d|]+z[w-v-r(w+v)]/2, (v-w)(1-z)/2-r(v+w)|d|}. Since r,u,v,w>0 both terms strictly decrease with |d|, every maximizer has x=y=(1-z)/2. The resulting lower envelope of f1(z)=-ru/2+[w-v+r(u-w-v)]z/2 and f3(z)=(v-w)(1-z)/2 gives the stated complete r=1 support classification including u=2v ties. For w<v,u>2v, f1<0<=f3, so the slope changes sign exactly at rc=(v-w)/(u-v-w) in (0,1), leading to z=0, arbitrary z, then z=1, although C is a strict pooled Condorcet loser. The exhibited twenty-ballot groups have exact margins (4/5,1/5,1/10), rc=1/5; rational LP implementation independently checks 625 finite parameter-grid inputs. All-r theorem is only claimed for this specified reversal region.

originality.rationale: PASS qualified. Khalaf et al. (2026) introduce robust maximal lotteries for variable population weights, prove robust Condorcet/dominance rules and a general linear programming characterization, all established and acknowledged. The inspected main text/appendix does not give the exact closed-form mirrored-opposed-winner support chambers or a strict pooled Condorcet loser becoming unique under increased uncertainty with a rational sharp radius. A generic finite LP is an algorithm for any instance, not an explicit all-positive-parameter classification, and the earlier fixed-majority maximal lotteries differ from a minimax range over θ. An unindexed application of the same LP could give an equivalent reversal; no absolute priority claimed.
